candidates.why: bit_write_CRC calls bit_chain_alloc(dat) at line 1375, which does realloc(dat->chain, ...) at line 3015 — realloc may free the old buffer and move it. Any pointer into the old dat->chain captured before line 1375 (e.g. by a caller passing a chain-derived address, or by code holding &dat->chain[x]) becomes dangling. Line 1384 re-reads dat->chain so this function is itself safe, but the realloc-invalidation contract is the classic hidden free-then-use vector for callers.

bit_write_RS(dat, crc) at line 1388 -> bit_write_RC (line 342) which calls bit_chain_alloc at lines 349-350 / 355-356, again realloc'ing dat->chain (line 3015). If the buffer is grown here, any chain pointer held by the caller across the bit_write_CRC call is invalidated. crc itself is a value so no direct dangling use, but the buffer relocation is a latent use-after-free for surrounding code.
